BMEris_ERS2HD.overview:
When a critical supplier cut off component deliveries to Nashan Diversified, the promising Hel design was left without a production path. Kallon Weapon Industries purchased the specifications and set about redesigning the chassis as a mobile skirmisher tailored for the perpetual low-intensity conflicts plaguing the former Free Worlds League. Rebranded the Eris (a reflection of the chaos and discord the design was intended to sow among its foes) the fifty-ton 'Mech entered production at Kallon's Loyalty facility around 3115.

Kallon's engineers distinguished the Eris from both the original Hel and their own popular Wolverine by dramatically enhancing the chassis's mobility in broken terrain, positioning the design as a direct competitor to Earthwerks' Phoenix Hawk line of mobile skirmishers and raiders. The redesign also replaced the Hel's armament with a more flexible weapons suite, giving MechWarriors greater adaptability across engagement ranges.
BMEris_ERS2HD.capabilities:
The Eris builds upon the Hel's proven N&D HLBM endo steel frame and Hermes 250 XL engine, retaining the fifty-ton chassis's excellent speed while dramatically enhancing mobility through the addition of Chilton 360 jump jets paired with a partial wing. This combination grants the Eris exceptional maneuverability in atmospheric operations, with jump performance rivaling many lighter 'Mechs, though the partial wing's effectiveness diminishes in thin atmospheres or vacuum conditions.

Offensively, the Eris centers its firepower around a Fusigon Smarttooth snub-nose particle projection cannon, trading the Hel's heavy PPC range for greater close-range damage potential. Paired Holly five-tube multi-missile launchers provide remarkable tactical flexibility, allowing MechWarriors to switch between long-range missile bombardment and close-range saturation fire as the engagement dictates. Three Diverse Optics small X-pulse lasers round out the armament, providing devastating accuracy at knife-fighting ranges.

Kallon Royalstar armor with CASE II protection across both side torsos shields the ammunition stores, mitigating the risk of catastrophic ammunition explosions. At approximately ninety-five percent of maximum armor coverage for the chassis, the Eris offers above-average protection for a medium 'Mech. The persistent vulnerability of the extralight engine to side torso destruction remains the design's most significant weakness, a tradeoff Kallon accepted to maintain the speed and payload necessary for the skirmisher role.
BMEris_ERS2HD.history:
The Eris proved well-suited to the chaotic political arena of the former Free Worlds League, where constant border disputes and factional conflicts created steady demand for mobile skirmishers. During the Dark Age, Kallon's Loyalty facility changed hands alongside the shifting allegiances of the region, passing through various splinter state governments before ultimately returning to Free Worlds League control when the nation reformed.

The Eris featured regularly in inter-League conflicts, perhaps most especially during the 3140 assault on Aitutaki by the Third Free Worlds Guards. Previous attempts to seize the agricultural world had faltered due to dense native jungles that limited ground-bound BattleMech mobility. Equipped with the Eris, the defending Sixteenth Regulan Hussars readily carried out hit-and-fade and pincer attacks against the bulk of the Guards, with the partial wing system excelling in the hostile environment. The Guards eventually countered by sending forward their own Erises and Phoenix Hawks to pin the Hussars for artillery and air strikes, ultimately eliminating the defenders and securing the world.

When the Fourth Regulan Hussars counter-attacked to reclaim Aitutaki, the Guards turned the Hussars' own pincer tactics against them, trapping the Fourth between salvaged 'Mechs from the Sixteenth and their main battle line. The Fourth was torn apart and forced to evacuate in disorder.

The fall of Thermopolis to Clan Wolf disrupted Wolverine production and created unexpected demand for the Eris family, particularly variants replicating the original Hel configuration that shared the Wolverine's tactical role. This development secured Kallon's position in the medium 'Mech market and ensured continued production well into the ilClan era.
BMEris_ERS2HD.deployment: The base Eris configuration, introduced around 3115, represents Kallon Weapon Industries' complete reimagining of the original Hel design. The addition of the Chilton 360 partial wing system defines the variant, providing enhanced mobility in broken terrain that distinguishes the Eris from its predecessor. Armed with a Fusigon Smarttooth snub-nose particle projection cannon, paired Holly multi-missile launchers, and three Diverse Optics small X-pulse lasers, this variant trades the Hel's raw long-range hitting power for superior tactical flexibility. This variant has seen extensive service across all Free Worlds League splinter states and remains in production at Kallon's Loyalty facility.

BMPhoenixHawkLAMMkII_PHXG1.overview: The PHX-G1 is a one-of-a-kind rebuild of a Star League-era Phoenix Hawk LAM Mk I, rebuilt with Clan weapons and electronics by an Internal Security Force black program in the 3140s. The Inner Sphere lost the ability to build Land-Air 'Mechs when the last LAM parts factory on Irece was destroyed, and by the ilClan era a working three-mode LAM is a museum piece. The ISF wanted deniable assets that could go anywhere with no DropShip to track: one pilot, one machine, no flag.
BMPhoenixHawkLAMMkII_PHXG1.capabilities: The PHX-G1 trades firepower for reach. As a standard three-mode LAM it can walk as a 'Mech, skim terrain in AirMech mode at up to 23 hexes a turn, or convert to a fighter with Safe Thrust 7. Seven improved jump jets give it 7 Jumping MP in 'Mech mode and set its thrust in Fighter mode. It reaches targets that ground forces cannot, and leaves before anyone can respond.
BMPhoenixHawkLAMMkII_PHXG1.deployment: There was only ever one PHX-G1. After the Kage no Tori purge, it appeared on the books of a yakuza gumi in the Buckminster Prefecture. It flew contraband between hidden airstrips and fought in unsanctioned arena bouts under a series of throwaway names. Since about 3149 it has operated freelance from a privately owned DropShip, taking bounty contracts across the Combine, the old Republic worlds and the Periphery border. Combine authorities have no official record of the machine. The ISF still wants it back.
BMPhoenixHawkLAMMkII_PHXG1.manufacturer: Kage no Tori Program (Internal Security Force)

DSUnionXHS_3071.overview:
The Union class DropShip is regarded as the yardstick against which all other military transports are measured. First launched in 2708, this 3,600-ton spheroid design has served as the standard company-level BattleMek carrier for over three centuries, capable of delivering twelve Meks and two aerospace fighters into the hottest landing zone. Produced in enormous numbers by shipyards across the Inner Sphere, the Union weathered the technological collapse of the Succession Wars far better than the larger and more complex transports it was often paired with, and has been in continuous production since its inception.

Smaller and more numerous than vessels like the Overlord or Colossus, the Union's combination of adequate capacity, proven reliability, and relative ease of manufacture has made it the most widely deployed military DropShip in the Inner Sphere. Its distinctive spheroid silhouette is recognized by soldiers and civilians alike on virtually every inhabited world, an enduring symbol of military power projection from the Periphery to the Clan homeworlds.
DSUnionXHS_3071.capabilities: The 3071 variant of the Union-X reconfigures the combined-arms loadout for a more infantry-heavy force structure, reducing Mek capacity to four cubicles while expanding battle armor bays to twelve and adding four heavy vehicle slots. Four fighter bays remain for aerospace support, and 335 tons of cargo space handles the increased supply needs of the larger embarked ground force. The expanded crew complement of 143 reflects the additional personnel required to support the vehicle and battle armor contingents. All other systems including the enhanced weapons array, 120 double heat sinks, 737 points of armor, and improved structural integrity remain identical to the original Union-X, making this a reconfiguration rather than a redesign.
DSUnionXHS_3071.history:
The Union class entered service in 2708 during the Star League era, designed by Boeing Interstellar to provide a standardized company-level Mek transport for the Star League Defense Force. The original vessels featured comparatively luxurious crew facilities including double-occupancy quarters and spacious recreation areas, reflecting the standards of the era. The design proved immediately successful and was adopted across the SLDF, with multiple manufacturers licensed to meet demand.

The Succession Wars that followed the Star League's collapse tested the Union's durability to its limits. As technological capabilities declined, a series of hydraulic and electrical malfunctions on later production vessels led designers to replace the original crew amenities with communal bunkrooms and multipurpose areas. These modifications also degraded the air circulation system, giving the Union and its larger cousin the Overlord a distinctive stale atmospheric taint that became notorious among their crews. Despite these compromises, the Union's fundamental soundness ensured it remained in production throughout the Succession Wars, though shortages of drive system replacement parts during the Third Succession War nearly ended the class's dominance.

The Clan Invasion of 3049 brought renewed urgency to modernization efforts. In July 3055, Federated-Boeing Interstellar launched a comprehensive refit featuring significantly upgraded weapons and a return to Star League-era crew facilities with double-occupancy cabins and improved air filtration. A terrorist incident at the Galax shipyards curtailed initial production, but the upgraded model eventually entered widespread service. The Clans independently developed the Union C, scaling the hull up to 4,700 tons with improved thrust and Clan-grade weapons to carry fifteen Meks in the Clan Trinary structure.

The Word of Blake Jihad spawned the most radical Union variant yet when the Blakists developed the Pocket WarShip conversion, mounting capital-grade missile launchers on a hull that appeared outwardly identical to the standard Union. These vessels attracted infamy during the Jihad for their shock appearances in engagements where defenders expected nothing more than a conventional transport. Meanwhile, the Shipil Company on Skye produced the Union-X, a 3,700-ton expansion that traded Mek capacity for additional fighter and battle armor bays to support the evolving combined-arms doctrine of the post-Clan Invasion era. The Union remains the most produced and widely distributed military DropShip in the Inner Sphere, with no sign of its dominance waning.
DSUnionXHS_3071.deployment: The 3071 variant of the Union-X entered service during the Jihad, configured for the infantry-heavy operations that characterized much of the fighting against the Word of Blake. Its expanded battle armor capacity made it particularly effective for urban combat and facility seizure operations where armored infantry could operate in environments too confined for BattleMeks.
